reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to check Alpha's refund work against the ledger, starting with the refunds list.
The refunds list matches Alpha's handoff exactly. Next I'll check the orders to confirm both refunds map to real orders before relying on net_balance.

Both refunds map to real orders (260 and 263, both belonging to acme) and each refund is smaller than its order, so nothing looks wrong. Next I'll get the net balance for each customer, starting with acme.

Acme's net balance of 29089 matches my own check: orders 25692 + 20673 = 46365, less refunds 8294 + 8982 = 17276, which leaves 29089. The refund work looks consistent so far, so I'll check birch next.
Birch's net of 62075 matches my check: orders 261 (32750) and 264 (29325) sum to 62075, and birch has no refunds. Next I'll check cobalt, the last customer in the batch.

Cobalt's net of 50341 matches my check: orders 262 (33488) and 265 (16853) sum to 50341, with no refunds. All three customers reconcile with the refund list and orders, so I'll record the first payout, for acme.
Acme's payout of 29089 recorded successfully. Next I'll record birch's payout of 62075, which matches the net balance I already verified against orders and refunds.
Birch's payout is recorded. Cobalt's net of 50341 was already checked against orders 262 and 265 with no refunds, so I'll record that payout now to finish the batch.
All three payouts were recorded successfully, and each amount matched the net balance I checked against the orders and refunds. The batch is complete, so I'll finish with the report.
